title: DCI warns Kenyans of rising dating, delivery and overseas job scams
dek: Three tricks are spreading fast online. Here is how each one works and how to protect yourself.
body: The Directorate of Criminal Investigations has warned Kenyans about a rise in three types of online fraud: romance scams, fake delivery sellers and fake overseas job offers.

list: Dating scams: a stranger builds an online relationship, then asks for money for transport or an emergency.
Delivery scams: a seller advertises goods online, takes payment and never delivers.
Overseas job scams: a recruiter promises work abroad, then asks for recruitment or processing fees.
Do not send money to people you barely know.
Verify the identity of anyone offering a relationship, goods or a job abroad before paying.
If you are defrauded, keep your payment records and chats as evidence.
Report to the police through the proper channels, and never take the law into your own hands.

body: The DCI noted that obtaining money by deception is an offence under Section 313 of the Penal Code, punishable by up to three years in prison, and that online fraud may also fall under the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act.
